title: Astronauts Reading Fan Mail
creator: NASA Johnson Space Center
summaryTr: NASA astronotları çocukların gönderdiği mektupları ve çizimleri okuyor: Uzayda peynir var mı? Tavuk nugget nasıl yenir? Astronotlar uzaylılara inanır mı? Samimi, esprili ve gerçek İngilizce konuşmalar.
levelNoteTr: B1, İngilizce altyazı desteğiyle dinleme için Lantern English tahminidir; resmî bir CEFR derecesi değildir. Yedi farklı astronot doğal ve hızlı konuşur; günlük ifadeler ve roket, yörünge gibi uzay kelimeleri vardır.

source.name: NASA — Astronauts Reading Fan Mail #3
source.license: Kamu malı (NASA yapımı, ABD'de telife tabi değil)

subtitleSource.name: NASA — resmî İngilizce SRT altyazısı
subtitleSource.changeNoteTr: NASA'nın tamamı büyük harfli altyazısı okunurluk için normal yazıma çevrildi, kısa parçalar cümle olarak birleştirildi ve bozuk kesme işaretleri düzeltildi; sözler korunmuştur.

captions.text: Hi, my name is Jeanette Epps.
Hi, I'm NASA astronaut, Kayla Barron.
I am NASA astronaut Kjell Lindgren, and I just got back from the International
Space Station a few weeks ago.
It's awesome to be back with my family and friends, to be back here on the Earth.
I do love to get real letters, whether it's at home or at work or even in space
we get cards and letters delivered from family from time to time, which is so exciting.
And this year we'd like to thank all the students who sent in letters and notes to us.
And this is one of my favorite things to do is to read your letters.
So let's get to it.
The first time you went into space, how did it feel?
Were you scared or happy?
My first space launch was incredible.
We were super well prepared, so I think for the most part we were just
executing the procedures, doing the job we had practiced doing.
But as we counted down, you know, the famous countdown from ten, nine, eight up to that
moment of launch, the rocket engines light underneath us.
And there's kind of this magic moment where you hang in the air, you're just off
the launch pad, and you can feel that you're starting to travel to space, but you haven't
really started accelerating yet.
And in that moment, I was just flooded with pure joy.
I was just so excited that my journey was finally starting and so excited to do it
with my teammates, my crew and our team around the world.
And so, yeah, it was I was happy more than anything else.
What do we have in here?
Look at this.
That's so good.
I'm going to put that on my refrigerator.
Oh, look at this.
This makes my day.
How great is that?
That's going up on the wall for sure.
I love those colors. Love it.
I had a bowl of cereal and milk for breakfast and chili for lunch.
And every now and then you open these up and you learn what, like,
somebody's favorite food is.
Is there cheese to eat in your spaceship?
I love cheese.
Oh, my gosh. Me too.
Actually, it's really hard to send cheese to space because it goes bad pretty quickly.
But you can send some hard cheeses to space, so I really hope that
that's there in my spaceship.
Sara says.
I think space is very cool, but I think space ice cream would be the best part.
Sara, you know all that there is to know because you're absolutely right, space
ice cream is very cool and cold.
Do you like chicken nuggets?
I love all chicken nuggets.
I'm sure there's somebody out there that does not like chicken nuggets,
but that is not me.
So I think the bigger chicken nugget question is, how do you eat your chicken nuggets?
With a fork, and knife, dip them in ketchup?
Are you kind of a mayonnaise or a mustard person?
Or is it just straight up, I've got 18 chicken nuggets in front of me
and I'm getting after it all right now?
So I don't care how you eat yours, but I'll tell you how I eat mine.
I definitely like chicken nuggets.
I like a little bit of ketchup and I definitely use my fingers.
It's a great question and I hope you have a wonderful holiday season, Charlie.
So what type of rocket ship did you go on?
Well, this most recent mission, I flew in a Crew Dragon capsule
on top of a Falcon-9 rocket.
It was absolutely amazing.
We launched from Kennedy Space Center and we were in low Earth orbit
in less than nine minutes.
Now, my first mission about seven years ago, I launched in a Soyuz capsule
on a Soyuz rocket out of baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
I launched with our Russian partners and, and that was my first flight.
And so it was really cool to have that experience of flying into space
on two different types of rockets.
What's your favorite thing about your job?
Well, Piper, one of my favorite things about my job is that I continue to learn new things
just about every day.
Flying in the T-38, doing robotics, just about everything that we do here.
There's always something new going on.
And I like to learn.
This is cool.
This is a launch pad.
Look at that.
Very detailed from Gabe.
Gabe, that's awesome.
I see.
We got the, we got the pad here.
We got the gantry that we walk across into the capsule there with the astronauts inside.
That is a great drawing, Gabe. Good job.
Can you feel heat in the spaceship?
Especially when we're coming home?
The- our spacecraft gets really hot.
That's why we have a heat shield that protects us as our spacecraft starts to travel
through the atmosphere.
Because all of that resistance of the gases in the atmosphere really cause the,
the craft to heat up.
But we're in suits that give us cooling, so they keep our bodies cool.
And it's kind of like you have air conditioning.
So even though the vehicle gets really hot, the spaceship gets really hot, we stay at a
comfortable temperature.
What types of things do we do in outer space?
Right now we're in low-Earth orbit, so that's where the space station is.
We do two main things there.
One is to keep it functioning and keep it working because it's a complex machine there
in low-Earth orbit.
The other thing we do is we do research there and a lot of our time
is trying to understand the human body, understand different things that we need to take
the next step to the Moon to stay and after that to Mars.
And so to keep exploring, we have to keep learning.
I love not knowing what is inside each of these letters.
And this one from Evan is really cool.
The drawings are always my favorite.
From Abigail in Saint George, Utah used a really awesome cat astronaut sticker here
who doesn't love a cat on a flying saucer?
Do astronauts believe in aliens?
Well, that's a good question.
I don't know.
Some maybe do and some maybe don't.
I think it would be amazing to discover aliens in our lifetime.
From my perspective, aliens probably don't look like little green men,
but they might be like tiny microorganisms that live or used to live on a planet
like Mars.
Unequivocally, 100%, I believe in aliens.
There is no way that you can be on the space station going around the Earth
and look out at night and see millions of stars and not think for certain.
There are aliens out there and people ask me if I've ever seen an alien.
And I say absolutely. 100%.
I've seen aliens because you're looking at them every night.
When you look out in the night sky, somewhere out there, there is some crazy civilization
doing some crazy work that we haven't discovered yet.
I know it is out there.
Thank you all so much for the letters that you write to us.
It means so much to receive them and I love reading every single one.
Thank you.
These letters are the rocket fuel that we use.
This is what keeps us going.
So please don't stop sending them, please keep sending them and help us push this
mission forward.
Because it's super important.
Thank you.
Thanks, everybody, for all your letters and your awesome questions.
The curiosity is awesome and I hope you stay engaged and thinking about how the world
and the universe works.
Thank you for your letters.
Keep them coming.
Have a great holiday.
I am so thankful to be back here on Earth with my family and friends
and I wish you all the best this holiday season as you spend time with your family,
with your friends on our incredible planet, our home, the Earth.
